name: FlowGuard — Gmail to Google Sheets
_comment: Gmail 'New Email' -> Google Sheets 'Create Spreadsheet Row', with dynamic
field mapping. Confirmed against the product by Janmejay, 2026-08-11.
__first__ means 'take whatever the product lists first'. Used where the
choice genuinely does not matter to the assertion (the Gmail account, the
mapping target column). The page object logs and records whichever value
it picked, so a failure stays reproducible.
The mapping TARGET is __first__ because the Sheets row fields are labelled
with the spreadsheet's own COLUMN HEADERS — on 'Trail' those were things
like 'From pricing yearly', 'Professional', 'IND'. They are data, not UI
copy, so pinning one by name would break the moment the sheet is edited.
source_field 'threadId' is a top-level scalar in the Gmail trigger's
sample payload, chosen because it is always present. Nested paths such as
payload.parts[1].filename exist in the sample too but the picker is a
flat list, so a nested key may not be selectable as one entry.
ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING, not stylistic:
- trigger.run_test must be true. The editor resolves mapping tokens
against the trigger's sample data, and that only exists after a run
test. utils/connect_spec rejects a spec that maps without it.
- Spreadsheet and Worksheet are dependent:true. The Sheets row fields
(data1, data2, ...) load asynchronously only after both settle; the
product allows itself 50s for that (see app-edit-options.component.ts
onCopilotSetFieldMapping). Mapping before they load is the single
biggest flake source in this flow.
